author: hoeschec
text:
So important to know the difference between Supply/Demand, FL, Origins, and ORFL

I am going to spend some time practicing this. Some of my posts last night are not correct.

Salivan says "S/D is a reaction to a FL"

He also says:Origins are created after S/D is created"

S/D, Origins, ORFl's, etc... exist on all time frames, in each scale. Understanding how to draw them (and why they are important) is a key part of keeping scale straight.

author: hoeschec
text:
EUR-GBP - More of the same analysis. Just looking in the past.

4-Hour chart back in 2012: We see the same patterns unfolding... over and over again.

The ORFL is hard to see in this scale...need to drop down to LTF.

Now look for ORFL - UP - In this scale...

Notice how every reaction to a FL creates a new supply/demand zone & Origin up/down... Look at the grey rectangle that shows ORFL - Down. When price comes back to test this zone, it reacts and creates supply. After the supply is created, there is an ORFL that forms (it forms on reaction to the newly created supply).

...And a new zone is born when price engulfs ORFL UP...look at the green rectangle to the very right of the chart.

Let's look closer at this new FL Box (shaded green)
